question: In a child with suspected infective endocarditis, at least two sets of blood cultures should be drawn from different sites BEFORE starting antibiotic therapy, because prior antibiotics reduce culture yield and may prevent accurate microbiological diagnosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The clinical pearl is: blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics. Pre-treated cases have far lower culture positivity, making pathogen identification (and therefore targeted therapy) impossible. This is the most commonly violated principle in IE management. Collect at least two sets from separate sites before initiating any antibiotic therapy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct and critical. Blood cultures before antibiotics is the single most important action in suspected IE. Antibiotic pre-treatment reduces blood culture positivity from approximately 95% to 50% or less. Draw 2-3 sets from separate venepuncture sites (not the same IV cannula) within 1-2 hours. Then start empirical antibiotics — do not delay indefinitely, but do not start before collecting cultures.
